figures.title: A risk becomes useful only when it becomes an owned response
figures.desc: A five-stage chain that turns a loose agent-work risk into a traced failure path, visible rating vector, enforceable response row, and explicitly owned residual risk.
figures.caption: Read left to right: naming danger starts the analysis; the row becomes operational only when the failure path, proof, response, and remaining exposure all have a place.
figures.transcript: Stage one records a loose risk such as wrong source or unauthorized action. Stage two separates cause, failure mode, local effect, and downstream effect. Stage three keeps severity, occurrence, and detection difficulty visible as an S/O/D vector with a severity override instead of hiding them in one product. Stage four adds the contract bearings: owner, preventive control, detection evidence, and recovery or rollback. Stage five records residual risk and either its authorized acceptance or the reason the task remains on hold.

figures.title: Place prevention, proof, and recovery along the failure path
figures.desc: A causal branch showing prevention before the failure mode, detection evidence between local and downstream effects, recovery for a detected state, and propagation when the state escapes.
figures.caption: Read from the cause: prevention blocks the mode; if the mode creates a local effect, evidence either intercepts it for recovery or misses it and allows downstream propagation.
figures.transcript: Begin with a credible cause or mechanism. A preventive control can block the failure mode before it occurs. If prevention fails, the function enters the failure mode and creates a local effect. Detection evidence is evaluated between that local effect and downstream propagation. When an inspectable artifact trips its failure condition, the named owner contains the state, restores known-good work, and decides whether restart is allowed. When detection is absent or misses, the local effect escapes into the downstream effect. This intercepted-versus-escaped branch is why detection evidence and recovery cannot be collapsed into one control claim.

figures.title: Five surfaces where a risk becomes orphaned
figures.desc: A diagnostic matrix mapping missing ownership, weak prevention, absent detection proof, missing recovery, and buried high severity to the reason each row is incomplete and the smallest corrective move.
figures.caption: Scan each row by signal, not by score; any one of these conditions can keep an apparently complete FMEA from becoming an operating contract.
figures.transcript: NO OWNER means nobody has the authority and access to act; assign a role and confirm authority. CONTROL IS PROSE means the stated safeguard does not identify a mechanism acting on the cause; replace it with a specific preventive control. NO DETECTION PROOF means a check is claimed without an artifact and passing condition; name both and test them. NO RECOVERY means detection can occur while the bad state persists; write containment, restoration, and restart authority. HIGH SEVERITY BURIED means an RPN product has obscured an S equals 5, irreversible, or unauthorized-authority effect; restore the S/O/D vector, apply the severity override, and hold until the response chain is complete or the proper authority accepts the residual risk.
